summary: Six small skills: one session governs while background agents take each goal to a pull request, keep a wiki current, run regression tests, and cut draft releases with manual verify steps. No engine: Markdown instructions and seven stdlib Python scripts.
use_cases: Take one sentence to a reviewed pull request
Run several goals in parallel and see what waits on you
Have a fresh agent judge a change it did not write
Cut a draft GitHub release with a changelog
Set up a repo's workflow config safely on a branch
Keep a GitHub wiki in the repo and find stale pages
Govern parallel goals from one session
Keep regression tests visible, with an issue per failure
writes: run state under the git common dir, in loop/ (never committed)
loop/runs/<slug>.design.txt and .design.json under the git common dir, when you run design.py
git worktrees under that loop/ folder
git branches loop/<slug> and workflow-setup, commits on them
VERSION and CHANGELOG.md on a goal's branch when you cut
pages it wrote, or that you name, in the repo's GitHub wiki, when you publish
a version bump commit on a goal's branch, only with pr_bumps_version on
loop/board.json, sessions.json, cadence and handoff.md under the git common dir, and a run record's note, retired mark or take-over, when you run board.py
loop/board.html, board-artifact.html and the finished sections of board.json, when you run board_page.py
loop/pocs/<slug>.md and .go under the git common dir, a POC's saved answer and go line, when you run batch.py
a batch heading and its poc lines in .loop/queue.md, when you run batch.py add
loop/waits/<slug> under the git common dir, when a goal is held by another
~/.workflow-loop/repos in the home folder, when you run board.py repos add
docs/wiki/*.md and a commit of them, when you run criteria.py review or sync --commit
network: github.com (git push, wiki push, gh pull request, issue and draft release calls, only when you run them)
the model host your own claude or codex command already uses
